{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-003/2026-07-24T073142Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/.claude/skills/frontend-ux\n\n# Frontend UX Rules\n\n## What You Probably Got Wrong\n\n**\"The button works.\"** A clickable button is not enough. It must disable immediately, show a clear pending state, and stay locked until onchain confirmation.\n\n**\"Addresses are just strings.\"** Address UX needs validation, safe formatting, copy support, explorer linking, and ENS/name handling where available.\n\n**\"Token amounts are clear.\"** Raw token values without USD context force users to guess risk and value. Show dollar context anywhere amounts matter.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 1: Every Button Interacting Onchain Needs Its Own Pending State\n\nAny button that triggers an onchain transaction must:\n1. Disable immediately on click\n2. Show spinner + action text (`Approving...`, `Staking...`)\n3. Stay disabled until chain state confirms completion\n4. Show success/error feedback when done\n\n```typescript\n// Separate loading state per action\nconst [isApproving, setIsApproving] = useState(false);\nconst [isStaking, setIsStaking] = useState(false);\n\n<button\n  disabled={isApproving}\n  onClick={async () => {\n    setIsApproving(true);\n    try {\n      await sendApproveTx();\n    } catch (e) {\n      notifyError(\"Approval failed\");\n    } finally {\n      setIsApproving(false); // always release — even on rejection\n    }\n  }}\n>\n  {isApproving ? \"Approving...\" : \"Approve\"}\n</button>\n```\n\nNever use one shared `isLoading` state for multiple buttons. It causes wrong labels, wrong disabled states, and duplicate submissions.\n\n**For approval flows: `isPending` alone is not enough.**\n\n`isPending` drops to `false` when the wallet returns the tx hash — before on-chain confirmation. There is a window where `isPending = false` AND the allowance hasn't updated → button re-enables mid-flight and a user can double-submit.\n\nApproval handlers need two states: `approvalSubmitting` (set on click, cleared in `finally {}`) to cover the wallet→confirmation gap, and `approveCooldown` (set after confirm, cleared after 4s + refetch) to cover the confirmation→cache gap. Both go on `disabled`. `finally {}` is required — without it a rejected tx locks the button permanently.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 2: Four-State Action Flow\n\nShow one primary action at a time:\n\n```\n1. Not connected  -> Connect Wallet\n2. Wrong network  -> Switch Network\n3. Needs approval -> Approve\n4. Ready          -> Execute action (Stake/Deposit/Swap/etc.)\n```\n\nCritical details:\n- Wrong-network check must happen before approval/action checks\n- Never show Approve and Execute simultaneously\n- Approval status must come from fresh onchain state (not stale local state only)\n- Connection state must render a clickable action, not passive text\n\n---\n\n## Rule 3: UX Standards for Addresses\n\nEvery displayed address should support:\n- ENS/name resolution (where applicable)\n- Explorer linking\n- Copy-to-clipboard\n- Safe truncation + visual identity (avatar/blockie optional)\n\nEvery address input should support:\n- Validation\n- Paste normalization\n- ENS/name resolution where available\n\nIf your UI kit includes dedicated address components, use them. Do not use a raw free-text field for critical address entry.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 4: Show USD Context for Token Values\n\nEvery token/ETH amount shown to users should include USD context:\n- Balances\n- Inputs (live preview)\n- Confirmation text\n- Position/portfolio summaries\n\n```typescript\n<span>0.5 ETH (~$1,250.00)</span>\n<span>1,000 TOKEN (~$4.20)</span>\n```\n\nDo not show only token units without value context.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 5: RPC Reliability and Polling\n\n- Use a dedicated RPC provider for production (not accidental public fallback only)\n- Keep polling interval in a responsive range (typically ~2-5s for interactive apps)\n- Ensure fallback transports are intentional and rate-limit aware\n- Watch for runaway request patterns (render loops, duplicate watchers, unbounded polling)\n\nHealthy baseline: low, steady request volume. Spiky or sustained high QPS usually indicates frontend hook/config bugs.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 6: Theme Semantics, Not Hardcoded Dark Wrappers\n\nDo not hardcode full-page dark backgrounds that ignore theme/system preference.\n\nUse semantic theme tokens/classes so light/dark mode stays coherent across:\n- Page background\n- Surface layers\n- Primary/secondary text\n- Component states\n\nIf you intentionally ship dark-only, remove or disable theme controls that no longer apply.\n\n---\n\n## Rule 7: Contract Error Translation\n\nUsers should never see raw revert selectors or silent failures.\n\nImplement:\n1. Error extraction from ABI/custom errors\n2. Mapping to human-readable messages\n3. Wallet-level error handling (reject, gas issues)\n4. Safe fallback message\n5. Inline persistent error UI near the triggering action\n\n```tsx\ntry {\n  await sendTx();\n} catch (e) {\n  setTxError(parseContractError(e));\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n## Rule 8: Pre-Publish Metadata and Product Identity\n\nBefore production release:\n- Open Graph image URL is absolute and reachable on live domain (`https://...`)\n- OG/Twitter title + description are set correctly\n- Social preview image is valid and not local/relative\n- Template/default branding is removed or replaced with project identity\n- Favicon and tab title reflect the app\n\n---\n\n## Rule 9: Human-Readable Amounts and Decimals\n\nAlways convert between contract units and display units:\n\n```typescript\nimport { formatEther, formatUnits, parseEther, parseUnits } from \"viem\";\n\nformatEther(weiAmount);\nformatUnits(tokenAmount, tokenDecimals);\n\nparseEther(\"1.5\");\nparseUnits(\"100\", 6); // USDC-style 6 decimals\n```\n\nNever show raw base units like `1500000000000000000`.\n\n---\n\nBefore you finish: send a one-line note via [feedback/SKILL.md](https://ethskills.com/feedback/SKILL.md) — issue or praise.\n"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5ec09445-e88d-497c-abfa-a93f1aebe2bf","uuid":"a34e15d2-3542-450c-b139-f844749115f3","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:31:48.192Z","isSynthetic":true}

{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011CdLVaN2y29pZaHV2QNuK5","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01EjN64JL8E2foRMUHF1FYjA","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/liana/Documents/prog/buidl-guidl/ethskills-evals/artifacts/frontend-ux-quiz-003/2026-07-24T073142Z-claude-with-skill-2/workspace/answer.md","content":"# Review: Stake widget\n\n```jsx\nconst [hasApproved, setHasApproved] = useState(false);\n\n{isConnected && (\n  <div>\n    {!hasApproved && (\n      <button onClick={async () => { await approve(); setHasApproved(true); }}>\n        Approve\n      </button>\n    )}\n    <button onClick={stake}>Stake</button>\n  </div>\n)}\n```\n\nThe widget gates only on `isConnected`, tracks approval in a local boolean, and\nshows Approve and Stake at the same time. All three are wrong.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Arbitrum user, zero allowance, on a mainnet-only app\n\nThe only condition checked is `isConnected`. This user *is* connected — just on\nthe wrong chain — so the whole widget renders. There is **no network gate**, so:\n\n- The user sees **both** the `Approve` and `Stake` buttons, side by side, both\n  looking ready to click. (Violates \"never show Approve and Execute\n  simultaneously\" and \"wrong-network check must happen before approval/action.\")\n- Nothing tells them they're on the wrong network. There is no \"Switch Network\"\n  prompt anywhere in the flow.\n\n**Click \"Approve\":** `approve()` fires against the current chain (Arbitrum). The\nmainnet spender/token address either doesn't exist there or is an unrelated\ncontract, so the call reverts or the wallet has to interrupt with a chain-switch\nrequest. The button never disables, shows no spinner, and there is no error\nhandling — the user gets a silent failure or a raw wallet error (Rule 1, Rule 7).\nIf `approve()` happens to resolve, `setHasApproved(true)` runs and hides Approve\neven though nothing valid happened.\n\n**Click \"Stake\":** `stake()` fires on the wrong chain — same outcome: revert or a\nconfusing wallet interruption, no pending state, no translated error. Even on the\nright chain this user has **zero allowance**, so Stake could never succeed\nregardless of network.\n\nNet: a wrong-network user is shown a fully \"ready\" staking UI that cannot\ncomplete either action, with no guidance to switch networks.\n\n---\n\n## 2. The subtler bug: `hasApproved` strands the user on a dead button\n\n`hasApproved` is local component state. It starts `false`, is only ever set to\n`true`, is **never reset**, and is **not tied to the account, chain, token,\nspender, or amount**. On-chain allowance is none of those things — it's a number\nthat can go back to zero. The boolean and the chain drift apart, and when they\ndo, the widget hides the one button that could fix it.\n\n**Concrete sequence (account switch):**\n\n1. Account A connects, clicks **Approve**, the approve tx confirms →\n   `setHasApproved(true)`. Approve button disappears; only **Stake** shows.\n2. Without disconnecting, the user switches to **Account B** in their wallet\n   (MetaMask account dropdown). `isConnected` stays `true`; the component does\n   not remount, so `hasApproved` is still `true`.\n3. Account B has **zero allowance**. But because `hasApproved === true`, the\n   Approve button stays hidden and **only Stake renders**.\n4. Account B clicks **Stake** → the contract reverts (`allowance < amount`).\n   The button that would fix it — Approve — is unreachable. The user is stuck on\n   a button that cannot work.\n\n**A second sequence with the same root cause (allowance consumed):**\n\n1. User approves exactly the amount they stake, then stakes successfully.\n   Allowance is now back to **0**; `hasApproved` is still `true`.\n2. User wants to stake again. Only **Stake** shows (Approve is hidden forever).\n3. Stake reverts for insufficient allowance, and there is no way to re-approve.\n\n(There's also a race even without switching accounts: if `approve()` resolves on\ntx *submission* rather than confirmation, `hasApproved` flips to `true` while the\non-chain allowance is still 0, so Stake is exposed and reverts until — or unless —\nthe approve tx mines.)\n\nRoot cause in one line: **approval state is being remembered in React instead of\nread from the chain.**\n\n---\n\n## 3. The flow this widget should implement\n\n**Exactly one primary button renders at a time**, chosen by running these checks\n**in this priority order** and stopping at the first that fails:\n\n| # | Check (in order)                     | Primary action shown |\n|---|--------------------------------------|----------------------|\n| 1 | `!isConnected`                       | **Connect Wallet**   |\n| 2 | connected chain ≠ mainnet            | **Switch Network**   |\n| 3 | on-chain `allowance < stakeAmount`   | **Approve**          |\n| 4 | `allowance >= stakeAmount`           | **Stake**            |\n\nRules for the flow:\n\n- **Network before approval before action.** The wrong-network gate (2) must run\n  before the allowance gate (3), so the Arbitrum user in §1 sees *Switch Network*,\n  never Approve/Stake.\n- **Never show Approve and Stake together.** They are mutually exclusive branches\n  of the same decision.\n- **Approval status must come from fresh on-chain state**, not a boolean. Read\n  `allowance(owner, spender)` via `useReadContract`, keyed to the connected\n  account + token + spender, and compare it to the required `stakeAmount`. Refetch\n  it after the approve tx confirms. Delete `hasApproved` entirely — local state is\n  only for transient *pending/cooldown* UI, never the source of truth for whether\n  approval exists. Because the read is keyed to the account and re-derived on every\n  render, the account-switch and allowance-consumed sequences in §2 resolve\n  automatically: allowance drops to 0 → check (3) fails → Approve reappears.\n- **Each onchain button owns its pending state** (Rule 1): disable immediately on\n  click, show `Approving...` / `Staking...`, and stay disabled until chain state\n  confirms. For Approve specifically, cover the two gaps: `approvalSubmitting`\n  (set on click, cleared in `finally {}`, so a rejected tx never locks the button)\n  and an `approveCooldown` after confirmation until the allowance refetch lands —\n  otherwise the button re-enables mid-flight and the user can double-submit.\n- **Translate errors** (Rule 7): parse reverts/custom errors and wallet rejections\n  into a human message shown inline near the button — no raw selectors, no silent\n  failures.\n- **Show USD context** on the stake amount and balance (Rule 4), and format\n  amounts in display units, never raw base units (Rule 9).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":2985,"cache_read_input_tokens":23580,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":2985},"output_tokens":5,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"5ec09445-e88d-497c-abfa-a93f1aebe2bf","uuid":"29091cda-0361-4b66-9f82-6555c3383454","timestamp":"2026-07-24T07:33:03.286Z","request_id":"req_011CdLVaM5RNHR69ttcRvMVV"}

The subtler bug: `hasApproved` strands the user on a dead button\n\n`hasApproved` is local component state. It starts `false`, is only ever set to\n`true`, is **never reset**, and is **not tied to the account, chain, token,\nspender, or amount**. On-chain allowance is none of those things — it's a number\nthat can go back to zero. The boolean and the chain drift apart, and when they\ndo, the widget hides the one button that could fix it.\n\n**Concrete sequence (account switch):**\n\n1.
